title: Quantum threat board: public evidence of how close a cryptographically relevant quantum computer is
policy: Every entry cites its primary source with a verbatim quote, the date it was published and the date it was checked. Vendor announcements are labelled as claims. Nothing here is scraped: an entry changes only when this file is edited and reviewed in git, and the file's SHA-256 is pinned in services/threat_board.py. Entries marked verified=false are listed but never charted or used in an estimate.

estimate.outer_bound_note: Morrow's own outer bound for the harvest clock's dial, not a survey answer.

changes.summary: First edition: 20 hardware milestones, 14 attack-cost estimates, 18 deadlines and 4 expert surveys, each checked against its primary source on 16 November 2026. The CRQC estimate (about 2035, likely by about 2040) comes from the Global Risk Institute 2025 survey, unchanged.

entries.title: Sycamore: 53 working qubits
entries.source_title: Quantum Supremacy Using a Programmable Superconducting Processor
entries.quote: we ran random hard circuits with 53 qubits and increasing depth
entries.note: Nature 574, 505 (2019). The chip has 54 qubits; 53 worked.

entries.title: Eagle: 127 qubits
entries.source_title: IBM Unveils Breakthrough 127-Qubit Quantum Processor
entries.quote: IBM today announced its new 127-quantum bit (qubit) 'Eagle' processor at the IBM Quantum Summit 2021

entries.title: Osprey: 433 qubits
entries.source_title: IBM Unveils 400 Qubit-Plus Quantum Processor and Next-Generation IBM Quantum System Two
entries.quote: The new 433 qubit 'Osprey' processor brings us a step closer to the point where quantum computers will be used

entries.title: 1,180 atoms loaded into a 1,225-site array
entries.source_title: Quantum startup Atom Computing first to exceed 1,000 qubits
entries.quote: a 1,225-site atomic array, currently populated with 1,180 qubits
entries.note: Atoms loaded into the array; not a benchmark of gates at that scale.

entries.title: Condor: 1,121 qubits
entries.source_title: IBM Quantum roadmap to 2033
entries.quote: We have introduced IBM Condor, a 1,121 superconducting qubit quantum processor based on our cross-resonance gate technology.

entries.title: 48 logical qubits from up to 280 atoms
entries.org: Harvard, MIT and QuEra (Bluvstein et al.)
entries.source_title: Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays
entries.quote: up to 48 logical qubits entangled with hypercube connectivity
entries.note: Nature, doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06927-3. The 48-qubit circuits detect errors and discard bad runs; they do not correct them. 280 is the most atoms used.

entries.title: 4 logical qubits from 30 physical qubits
entries.source_title: How Microsoft and Quantinuum achieved reliable quantum computing
entries.quote: four highly reliable logical qubits from only 30 physical qubits
entries.note: The preprint (arXiv:2404.02280) says the 800-fold improvement relies on post-selection.

entries.title: 12 logical qubits on a 56-qubit machine
entries.source_title: Microsoft and Quantinuum create 12 logical qubits and demonstrate a hybrid, end-to-end chemistry simulation
entries.quote: 12 highly reliable logical qubits
entries.note: 56 is the machine's size, not a stated count of qubits used for the encoding.

entries.title: 28 logical qubits from 112 atoms
entries.source_title: Microsoft and Atom Computing offer a commercial quantum machine with the largest number of entangled logical qubits on record
entries.quote: Twenty-eight logical qubits, created from 112 physical qubits, were used to perform successful computations
entries.note: The same post reports 24 logical qubits entangled in a cat state.

entries.title: Willow: errors fall as the code grows (below threshold)
entries.source_title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
entries.quote: 0.143% ± 0.003% error per cycle of error correction
entries.note: Nature 638, 920 (2025). One logical memory qubit, not logical computation. 105 is the chip's size (announced 9 December 2024).

entries.title: Ocelot: 5 cat data qubits
entries.source_title: Amazon announces Ocelot quantum chip
entries.quote: five data qubits (the cat qubits)
entries.note: Cat qubits are a different kind of qubit; the count is not comparable with the others, so it is not charted.

entries.title: Majorana 1: eight topological qubits, claimed
entries.source_title: Microsoft's Majorana 1 chip carves new path for quantum computing
entries.quote: Today, the company has placed eight topological qubits on a chip designed to scale to one million.
entries.note: Disputed. The accompanying Nature paper (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-08445-2) reports results only 'consistent with' Majorana modes, and does not demonstrate topological qubits. Not charted.

entries.title: Below-threshold error correction with up to 448 atoms
entries.org: Harvard, MIT and QuEra (Bluvstein et al.)
entries.source_title: Architectural mechanisms of a universal fault-tolerant quantum computer
entries.quote: 2.14(13)x below-threshold performance in a four-round characterization circuit
entries.note: Nature, doi:10.1038/s41586-025-09848-5. Date is the first arXiv version.

entries.title: 6,100 atoms held in a tweezer array
entries.source_title: A tweezer array with 6100 highly coherent atomic qubits
entries.quote: trapping over 6,100 neutral atoms in around 12,000 sites
entries.note: Nature 647, 60 (2025). Atoms are held and kept coherent; no gates between them were shown.

entries.title: Two-qubit gates above 99.99% fidelity
entries.source_title: IonQ Achieves Landmark Result, Setting New World Record in Quantum Computing Performance
entries.quote: IonQ has achieved the world's highest two-qubit gate performance, with fidelity exceeding 99.99%
entries.note: A gate fidelity on prototype hardware, not a system qubit count.

entries.title: Helios: 98 qubits, 48 error-corrected logical qubits
entries.source_title: Quantinuum announces commercial launch of new Helios quantum computer
entries.quote: 48 LQ (error corrected) with better than physical performance (99.99% state prep and measurement fidelity).
entries.note: The same release counts 94 and 50 logical qubits that are error-detected only; the board uses the 48 error-corrected.

entries.title: Nighthawk: 120 qubits
entries.source_title: IBM Delivers New Quantum Processors, Software, and Algorithm Breakthroughs on Path to Advantage and Fault Tolerance
entries.quote: 120 qubits linked together with 218 next-generation tunable couplers

entries.title: Roadmap: 200 logical qubits by 2029
entries.source_title: IBM Sets the Course to Build World's First Large-Scale, Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer
entries.quote: 100 million quantum operations using 200 logical qubits
entries.note: A plan, not a result: Starling is to be delivered by 2029. Not charted.

entries.title: Magic-state cultivation: 40-fold fewer errors
entries.source_title: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing
entries.quote: achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states
entries.note: Prepares the special states fault-tolerant algorithms such as Shor's need. Reported as published in Science; the board cites Google's own post.

entries.title: Helios: 99.9995% logical fidelity
entries.source_title: Quantinuum Breaks Error-Correction World Record by 10x
entries.quote: achieving a logical fidelity of 99.9995% on its Helios commercial computer.
entries.note: Not peer-reviewed at the time of checking.

entries.title: Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
entries.source_title: Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
entries.quote: the full quantum computer needs about a billion physical qubits, operating for about one day.
entries.assumptions: Error rate a tenth of the surface-code threshold; 100 ns measurements; a 2000-bit number.

entries.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits
entries.source_title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits
entries.quote: When factoring 2048 bit RSA integers, our construction's spacetime volume is a hundredfold less than comparable estimates from earlier works
entries.assumptions: 0.1% physical gate error, 1 µs surface-code cycle, 10 µs reaction time, nearest-neighbour grid.
entries.note: Quantum 5, 433 (2021). The figure is in the title.

entries.title: Reducing the Number of Qubits in Quantum Factoring
entries.source_title: Reducing the Number of Qubits in Quantum Factoring
entries.quote: To factor an RSA-2048 instance, we estimate that 1730 logical qubits and $2^{36}$ Toffoli gates will suffice for a single run, and the algorithm needs on average 40 runs.
entries.note: CRYPTO 2025 (revised).

entries.title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
entries.source_title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
entries.quote: I estimate that a 2048 bit RSA integer could be factored in less than a week by a quantum computer with less than a million noisy qubits.
entries.assumptions: 0.1% uniform gate error, 1 µs surface-code cycle, 10 µs reaction time, nearest-neighbour grid.
entries.note: The paper's own total is 897,864 physical qubits.

entries.title: Resource Analysis of Low-Overhead Transversal Architectures for Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
entries.org: Zhou, Duckering, Zhao, Bluvstein, Cain, Kubica, Wang, Lukin
entries.source_title: Resource Analysis of Low-Overhead Transversal Architectures for Reconfigurable Atom Arrays
entries.quote: finding that 2048-bit RSA factoring can be executed with 19 million qubits in 5.6 days, for 1 ms QEC cycle times.
entries.assumptions: Neutral-atom arrays with transversal gates; 1 ms error-correction cycle.
entries.note: ISCA 2025.

entries.title: The Pinnacle Architecture: Reducing the cost of breaking RSA-2048 to 100 000 physical qubits using quantum LDPC codes
entries.source_title: The Pinnacle Architecture: Reducing the cost of breaking RSA-2048 to 100 000 physical qubits using quantum LDPC codes
entries.quote: We find that fewer than one hundred thousand physical qubits are required for factoring at a physical error rate of p = 10-3 in an expected runtime of one month.
entries.assumptions: 0.1% physical error, 1 µs cycle, 10 µs reaction time; quantum LDPC codes, which need longer-range connections than a flat grid.
entries.note: A company's preprint, not yet peer-reviewed.

entries.title: Quantum resource estimates for computing elliptic curve discrete logarithms
entries.source_title: Quantum resource estimates for computing elliptic curve discrete logarithms
entries.quote: our simulation of the point addition quantum circuit for the NIST standardized curve P-256 needs 2330 logical qubits
entries.note: ASIACRYPT 2017.

entries.title: Improved quantum circuits for elliptic curve discrete logarithms
entries.source_title: Improved quantum circuits for elliptic curve discrete logarithms
entries.quote: for solving the ECDLP on a 256-bit elliptic curve, we reduce the number of qubits from 2338 to 2124
entries.note: PQCrypto 2020.

entries.title: The Impact of Hardware Specifications on Reaching Quantum Advantage in the Fault Tolerant Regime
entries.source_title: The Impact of Hardware Specifications on Reaching Quantum Advantage in the Fault Tolerant Regime
entries.quote: To break the encryption instead within one day it would require 13 million physical qubits.
entries.assumptions: Surface code, 1 µs cycle, 10 µs reaction time, 0.1% physical gate error; Bitcoin's secp256k1.
entries.note: AVS Quantum Science 4 (2022); first on arXiv 27 August 2021. Within one hour: about 317 million.

entries.title: Computing 256-bit Elliptic Curve Logarithm in 9 Hours with 126133 Cat Qubits
entries.org: Gouzien, Ruiz, Le Régent, Guillaud, Sangouard
entries.source_title: Performance Analysis of a Repetition Cat Code Architecture: Computing 256-bit Elliptic Curve Logarithm in 9 Hours with 126133 Cat Qubits
entries.quote: such an architecture can compute a 256-bit elliptic curve logarithm in 9 h with 126133 cat qubits
entries.assumptions: Cat qubits with a repetition code; 500 ns cycle; one-photon to two-photon loss ratio 1e-5.
entries.note: Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 040602 (2023). Cat qubits are not comparable one-for-one with surface-code qubits.

entries.title: How to compute a 256-bit elliptic curve private key with only 50 million Toffoli gates
entries.source_title: How to compute a 256-bit elliptic curve private key with only 50 million Toffoli gates
entries.quote: one key can be generated every 10 minutes using 6000 modules with 1152 physical qubits each.
entries.assumptions: Photonic-style active-volume architecture with non-local connections, 10 µs cycle.
entries.note: Counts modules, not a single qubit total, so it is not charted.

entries.title: Reducing the Number of Qubits in Quantum Discrete Logarithms on Elliptic Curves
entries.source_title: Reducing the Number of Qubits in Quantum Discrete Logarithms on Elliptic Curves
entries.quote: For $n = 256$ we estimate that 1193 qubits would be necessary, with 22 independent runs
entries.note: EUROCRYPT 2026. Some later papers quote 1098 for this work; the board uses the abstract's figure.

entries.title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates and Mitigations
entries.org: Babbush, Zalcman, Gidney et al. (Google Quantum AI)
entries.source_title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates and Mitigations
entries.quote: those circuits can execute in minutes using fewer than half a million physical qubits.
entries.assumptions: Superconducting qubits, 0.1% physical error, planar connectivity; secp256k1.
entries.note: The circuits are withheld and checked with a zero-knowledge proof. Logical qubits: fewer than 1,200 (with fewer than 90 million Toffoli gates).

entries.title: Quantum Algorithm for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms with Space-Efficient Point Addition
entries.org: Luo, Yang, Luo, Wang, Su, Sun, Li, Li
entries.source_title: Quantum Algorithm for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms with Space-Efficient Point Addition
entries.quote: For a 256-bit prime-field curve, our construction requires only 835 logical qubits
entries.assumptions: Logical level only; uses mid-circuit measurement.

entries.title: NIST publishes the first post-quantum standards
entries.source_title: Post-Quantum Cryptography FIPS Approved
entries.quote: The Secretary of Commerce has approved three Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) for post-quantum cryptography
entries.what: ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) became standards.

entries.title: US goal: mitigate quantum risk by 2035
entries.source_title: National Security Memorandum 10
entries.quote: with the goal of mitigating as much of the quantum risk as is feasible by 2035
entries.what: Mitigate as much quantum risk as feasible across US systems.

entries.title: NIST deprecates RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography after 2030
entries.source_title: NIST IR 8547, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
entries.quote: NIST will deprecate quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography after 2030 and disallow its use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.
entries.what: RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, Diffie-Hellman and ECDH become deprecated: still allowed, but on the way out.
entries.note: The final version (27 October 2026) applies this at every security strength; the 2024 draft distinguished 112-bit strength.

entries.title: NIST disallows RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography after 2035
entries.source_title: NIST IR 8547, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
entries.quote: NIST will deprecate quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography after 2030 and disallow its use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.
entries.what: Quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms are no longer allowed under NIST standards.

entries.title: US agencies support TLS 1.3
entries.source_title: Executive Order 14306
entries.quote: as soon as practicable, but not later than January 2, 2030
entries.what: Federal agencies support TLS 1.3 or a successor.

entries.title: US high-value systems use post-quantum key establishment
entries.source_title: Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
entries.quote: transition all HVAs and high impact systems to use PQC for key establishment by December 31, 2030;
entries.what: Federal high-value assets and high-impact systems switch key establishment to post-quantum.

entries.title: US agencies mitigate as much quantum risk as feasible
entries.org: US Office of Management and Budget
entries.source_title: OMB M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
entries.quote: with the objective of mitigating as much quantum risk as feasible by December 31, 2030.
entries.what: Federal civilian agencies run a risk-prioritised migration.

entries.title: US high-value systems use post-quantum signatures
entries.source_title: Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
entries.quote: transition all HVAs and high impact systems to use PQC for digital signatures by December 31, 2031;
entries.what: Federal high-value assets and high-impact systems switch digital signatures to post-quantum.

entries.title: US agencies complete the migration
entries.org: US Office of Management and Budget
entries.source_title: OMB M-26-15, Execution of the Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography
entries.quote: The final phase should focus on completing the migration of remaining systems
entries.what: All remaining federal civilian systems are migrated (phase 5).

entries.title: UK: discovery and a migration plan
entries.source_title: NCSC, Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
entries.quote: Carry out a full discovery exercise
entries.what: Define migration goals, find what uses vulnerable cryptography, and build an initial plan.

entries.title: UK: highest-priority migrations done
entries.source_title: NCSC, Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
entries.quote: Carry out your early, highest-priority PQC migration activities
entries.what: Finish the highest-priority migrations and refine the plan into a full roadmap.

entries.title: UK: migration complete
entries.source_title: NCSC, Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
entries.quote: Complete migration to PQC of all your systems, services and products
entries.what: Every system, service and product is migrated.

entries.title: EU: first steps in every member state
entries.source_title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
entries.quote: By 31.12.2026: At least the First Steps have been implemented by all Member States.
entries.what: Member states start national roadmaps, inventories and pilots.

entries.title: EU: high-risk uses migrated
entries.source_title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
entries.quote: The PQC transition for high-risk use cases has been completed.
entries.what: High-risk use cases are migrated; vulnerable public-key mechanisms are not used on their own there.

entries.title: EU: medium-risk uses migrated
entries.source_title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
entries.quote: By 31.12.2035: The PQC transition for medium-risk use cases has been completed.
entries.what: Medium-risk use cases are migrated, and low-risk ones as far as feasible.

entries.title: Canada: departmental migration plans
entries.source_title: Roadmap for the migration to post-quantum cryptography for the Government of Canada (ITSM.40.001)
entries.quote: April 2026: Develop an initial departmental PQC migration plan
entries.what: Each federal department has an initial migration plan.

entries.title: Canada: high-priority systems migrated
entries.source_title: Roadmap for the migration to post-quantum cryptography for the Government of Canada (ITSM.40.001)
entries.quote: End of 2031: Completion of PQC migration of high priority systems

entries.title: Canada: remaining systems migrated
entries.source_title: Roadmap for the migration to post-quantum cryptography for the Government of Canada (ITSM.40.001)
entries.quote: End of 2035: Completion of PQC migration of remaining systems
entries.what: All remaining federal systems are migrated.

entries.title: Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025
entries.org: Global Risk Institute (Mosca and Piani, evolutionQ)
entries.source_title: Global Risk Institute, Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025
entries.quote: Survey respondents believe the quantum threat is 'looming,' with a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) quite possible (28-49%) within the next 10 years, and likely (51-70%) in the next 15.
entries.question: a quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 within 24 hours
entries.note: Each range runs from a pessimistic to an optimistic reading of the experts' answers, averaged across them.

entries.title: Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2024
entries.org: Global Risk Institute (Mosca and Piani, evolutionQ)
entries.source_title: Global Risk Institute, 2024 Quantum Threat Timeline Report
entries.quote: An "optimistic" interpretation of the responses ... leads on average to a ~34% estimate of a CRQC being developed within a decade
entries.question: a quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 within 24 hours

entries.title: Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2023
entries.org: Global Risk Institute (Mosca and Piani, evolutionQ)
entries.source_title: Global Risk Institute, 2023 Quantum Threat Timeline Report
entries.quote: the average probability associated by the above-described analysis to the disruptive quantum threat is already ~17% in the next 10 years
entries.question: a quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 within 24 hours
entries.note: Only the pessimistic reading is stated in the text for this edition.

entries.title: 2022 Quantum Threat Timeline Report
entries.org: Global Risk Institute (Mosca and Piani, evolutionQ)
entries.source_title: Global Risk Institute, 2022 Quantum Threat Timeline Report
entries.quote: the probability associated by the above-described analysis to the disruptive quantum threat is already ~10% in the next 10 years (~27% for the optimistic interpretation)
entries.question: a quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 within 24 hours
